question: 93 + 74 − 58 + (33 + 18) × 2 − 102 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 109.

GIVEN

• 93 + 74 − 58 + (33 + 18) × 2 − 102

SOLUTION

• Bracket first: (33 + 18) = 51.

• Multiply (BODMAS): 51 × 2 = 102.

• Now: 93 + 74 − 58 + 102 − 102 = 167 − 58 + 102 − 102 = 109 = 109.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Notice the +102 and −102 cancel out, so you only need 93 + 74 − 58 = 109 instantly.

NOTE

• Always follow BODMAS: Brackets → Of/Orders → Division → Multiplication → Addition → Subtraction.

question: 88 + 26 − 42 + (17 × 2) + 33 ÷ 3 − 14 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 103.

GIVEN

• 88 + 26 − 42 + (17 × 2) + 33 ÷ 3 − 14

SOLUTION

• Bracket & division first: (17 × 2) = 34 and 33 ÷ 3 = 11.

• Now: 88 + 26 − 42 + 34 + 11 − 14.

• = 114 − 42 + 34 + 11 − 14 = 72 + 34 + 11 − 14 = 103 = 103.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Add all + terms (88+26+34+11 = 159) and all − terms (42+14 = 56); 159 − 56 = 103.

NOTE

• In BODMAS, resolve ÷ and × before doing + and − even without brackets.

question:
The line chart given below shows the total number of athletes representing a country in 5 consecutive Asian Games AG1, AG2, AG3, AG4 and AG5.

Which Asian games shows highest increase in number of athletes over the just previous games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. AG4.

GIVEN

• Athletes: AG1 = 254, AG2 = 268, AG3 = 302, AG4 = 356, AG5 = 384.

SOLUTION

• Increase over previous games:

• AG2 = 268 − 254 = 14; AG3 = 302 − 268 = 34; AG4 = 356 − 302 = 54; AG5 = 384 − 356 = 28.

• Largest jump = 54 at AG4.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Just eyeball the steepest rise on the line; the longest upward step is between AG3 and AG4.

NOTE

• 'Increase over previous' means consecutive differences — compare gaps, not the absolute heights.

question:
The line chart given below shows the monthly petrol consumption (in litres) by 6 different cars CR1, CR2, CR3, CR4, CR5 and CR6.

The price of petrol is Rs. 95 per litre. What is the total monthly expenditure (in Rs.) on petrol for cars CR4, CR5 and CR6 together?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 20045.

GIVEN

• Consumption: CR4 = 60 L, CR5 = 76 L, CR6 = 75 L; price = Rs. 95 per litre.

SOLUTION

• Total litres = 60 + 76 + 75 = 211 L.

• Expenditure = 211 × 95 = Rs. 20045 = 20045.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• 211 × 95 = 211 × 100 − 211 × 5 = 21100 − 1055 = 20045.

NOTE

• Multiplying by 95 = ×100 minus ×5; a fast way to handle 'near-100' multipliers.

question:
The pie chart given below shows the marks obtained by a student in the 6 subjects. The data is presented in the terms of degrees.

Total marks obtained by the student in the given 6 subjects = 600.

Marks obtained in A are what percent of marks obtained in C?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 166.67%.

GIVEN

• A = 90°, C = 54° (total 360° = 600 marks).

SOLUTION

• Marks are proportional to degrees, so ratio A : C = 90 : 54.

• Required % = (90 ÷ 54) × 100 = (5 ÷ 3) × 100 = 166.67% = 166.67%.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Skip converting to marks; degrees alone give it: 90/54 = 5/3 = 166.67%.

NOTE

• In a pie chart, each sector's value is directly proportional to its angle, so ratios of angles = ratios of values.

question:
The bar graph given below shows the marks obtained by the given 5 students in English.

Marks obtained by T are what percent more than the marks obtained by S?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 25%.

GIVEN

• Marks: T = 75, S = 60.

SOLUTION

• Difference = 75 − 60 = 15.

• Percent more = (15 ÷ 60) × 100 = 25% = 25%.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• 15 is one-fourth of 60, and 1/4 = 25% directly.

NOTE

• 'A is what percent more than B' = ((A − B)/B) × 100 — always divide by the base value B.

question:
The bar graph given below shows the number of boys (B) and girls (G) in 5 given schools.\

R = Total number of boys in the given 5 schools.

T = Average number of girls in the given 5 schools.

What is the value of R − T?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 468.

GIVEN

• Boys: 100, 120, 180, 60, 140. Girls: 80, 160, 100, 120, 200.

SOLUTION

• R = total boys = 100 + 120 + 180 + 60 + 140 = 600.

• Girls total = 80 + 160 + 100 + 120 + 200 = 660, so T = 660 ÷ 5 = 132.

• R − T = 600 − 132 = 468 = 468.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Add boys and girls totals mentally in pairs (200+180+240 etc.); then divide only the girls' total by 5.

NOTE

• Average = (sum of all values) ÷ (number of values); keep 'total' and 'average' clearly separate in DI questions.

question: Four numbers are in the ratio 1:2:3:4. Their sum is 16. Calculate the sum of the first and fourth numbers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 8.

GIVEN

• Four numbers in ratio 1 : 2 : 3 : 4, sum = 16.

SOLUTION

• Total ratio parts = 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10, so 1 part = 16 ÷ 10 = 1.6.

• First = 1.6, fourth = 4 × 1.6 = 6.4.

• Sum of first and fourth = 1.6 + 6.4 = 8 = 8.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• First + fourth = (1 + 4) parts = 5 parts, and 5 parts = (5/10) × 16 = 8.

NOTE

• In ratio problems, value of any group = (its parts ÷ total parts) × total sum.

question: Find the approximate value of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 59.

GIVEN

• (270.12 × ∛215.97) ÷ (2.96 × √80.93) − (9.92 + 3.08) ÷ √168.91

SOLUTION

• Round: ∛215.97 ≈ 6, √80.93 ≈ 9, √168.91 ≈ 13, 270.12 ≈ 270, 2.96 ≈ 3.

• First term = (270 × 6) ÷ (3 × 9) = 1620 ÷ 27 = 60.

• Second term = (9.92 + 3.08) ÷ 13 = 13 ÷ 13 = 1.

• Value ≈ 60 − 1 = 59 = 59.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Replace every number by its nearest perfect cube/square (216, 81, 169) to turn ugly decimals into clean integers.

NOTE

• For approximation questions, round to the nearest perfect power: ∛216 = 6, √81 = 9, √169 = 13.

question: Find the value of .
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 91.

GIVEN

• (49² − 42²) ÷ 7

SOLUTION

• Use a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b): 49² − 42² = (49 + 42)(49 − 42) = 91 × 7.

• Divide by 7: (91 × 7) ÷ 7 = 91 = 91.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• The (49 − 42) = 7 factor cancels the ÷7, leaving just (49 + 42) = 91.

NOTE

• a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b) is one of the most time-saving identities in SSC arithmetic.

question: What is the average of the first 28 multiples of 17?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 246.5.

GIVEN

• First 28 multiples of 17.

SOLUTION

• Average of first n multiples of x = x × (n + 1) ÷ 2.

• = 17 × (28 + 1) ÷ 2 = 17 × 29 ÷ 2 = 493 ÷ 2 = 246.5 = 246.5.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Just compute 17 × 14.5 (since (28+1)/2 = 14.5) = 246.5 in one step.

NOTE

• Average of first n multiples of x = x(n + 1)/2; average of first n natural numbers = (n + 1)/2.

question: Which of the following is smaller than ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 0.77̄ (0.7777…).

GIVEN

• Reference value 0.79̄ = 0.797979…

SOLUTION

• Expand each option: 0.81̄ = 0.8111…, 0.88̄ = 0.8888…, 0.77̄ = 0.7777…, 0.82̄ = 0.8222…

• Compare with 0.7979…: only 0.7777… is less than 0.7979…

• Hence the smaller value = 0.7777….

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• The reference starts 0.79, so anything starting 0.8… is already bigger; only the 0.77… option can be smaller.

NOTE

• To compare repeating decimals, write out a few digits (0.7777…, 0.7979…) and compare place by place.

question:
The table given below shows the number of pens in the 8 shops.

What are the total number of pens in A, B, C and H?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 1800.

GIVEN

• A = 100, B = 800, C = 200, H = 700.

SOLUTION

• Total = 100 + 800 + 200 + 700.

• = 900 + 900 = 1800 = 1800.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Pair for round sums: (100 + 800) = 900 and (200 + 700) = 900; add to get 1800.

NOTE

• In table DI, pick only the rows asked; pairing numbers into round hundreds speeds addition.

question:
The table given below shows the number of pens of type P1, P2, P3 and P4 manufactured by 2 factories F and G.

What are the average number of P3 type pens manufactured by F and G?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 120.

GIVEN

• P3 pens: F = 140, G = 100.

SOLUTION

• Average = (140 + 100) ÷ 2.

• = 240 ÷ 2 = 120 = 120.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Average of two numbers = their midpoint; halfway between 140 and 100 is 120.

NOTE

• Read only the P3 column; average of two values = (a + b)/2.

question: The sum of the three consecutive even numbers is 42. What is the smallest of the three numbers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 12.

GIVEN

• Three consecutive even numbers sum to 42.

SOLUTION

• Let them be x, x + 2, x + 4: x + (x + 2) + (x + 4) = 42.

• 3x + 6 = 42 → 3x = 36 → x = 12.

• Smallest = 12 (numbers 12, 14, 16).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Middle number = sum ÷ 3 = 42 ÷ 3 = 14; smallest = 14 − 2 = 12.

NOTE

• For any odd count of numbers in AP, the middle term = total sum ÷ count.

question: What is the remainder when 5837 is divided by 11?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 7.

GIVEN

• 5837 ÷ 11.

SOLUTION

• 11 × 530 = 5830, and 5837 − 5830 = 7.

• So the remainder = 7.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Alternating digit sum from right: 7 − 3 + 8 − 5 = 7; that value (0–10) is the remainder mod 11.

NOTE

• Divisibility/remainder by 11 uses the alternating sum of digits; if it is negative, add 11.

question: 95P9 is divisible by 11. What is the value of P?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 5.

GIVEN

• Number 95P9 divisible by 11.

SOLUTION

• Alternating sum (odd-place − even-place from right): (9 + 5) − (P + 9) = 5 − P.

• For divisibility by 11, this must be 0 (or a multiple of 11): 5 − P = 0.

• So P = 5.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Set (sum of alternate digits) equal: 9 + 5 = P + 9 → P = 5 straight away.

NOTE

• A number is divisible by 11 when the difference of alternate digit sums is 0 or a multiple of 11.

question: Two straight lines CD and AB cut each other at point O. Angle AOD = 75 degrees. What is the value (in degrees) of angle AOC?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 105.

GIVEN

• Lines AB and CD meet at O; ∠AOD = 75°.

SOLUTION

• ∠AOD and ∠AOC lie on the straight line CD, so they form a linear pair.

• ∠AOC = 180° − ∠AOD = 180° − 75° = 105° = 105.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Angles on a straight line add to 180°, so just do 180 − 75 = 105.

NOTE

• Linear pair: adjacent angles on a straight line sum to 180°; vertically opposite angles are equal.

question: Average age of 5 boys is 15 years. Average age of 10 girls is 12 years. What is the combined average age (in years) of these boys and girls?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 13.

GIVEN

• 5 boys average 15 yr; 10 girls average 12 yr.

SOLUTION

• Total age of boys = 5 × 15 = 75; total age of girls = 10 × 12 = 120.

• Combined average = (75 + 120) ÷ (5 + 10) = 195 ÷ 15 = 13 = 13.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Weighted mean = (5×15 + 10×12)/15; since girls (weight 10) dominate, answer sits near 12, i.e. 13.

NOTE

• Combined average = (sum of all quantities) ÷ (total count), never the simple average of the two averages.

question: In the given figure, AB is parallel to CD. Angle PAB = 55 degrees and angle DCP = 115 degrees. What is the value (in degrees) of angle APC?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 60.

GIVEN

• AB ∥ CD, ∠PAB = 55°, ∠DCP = 115°.

SOLUTION

• Draw a line through P parallel to AB and CD.

• ∠DCP = 115° gives the angle of PC with the horizontal as 180° − 115° = 65° (alternate angle at P).

• ∠PAB = 55° gives the angle of PA with the horizontal as 55° (alternate angle at P).

• ∠APC = 65° − 55° = 60° = 60.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• With AB ∥ CD, ∠APC = ∠DCP − ∠PAB = 115° − 55° = 60°.

NOTE

• Drawing an auxiliary line through the vertex parallel to the two given parallels splits the angle into two alternate angles.
